[1/2] Review the last 12 pushes: honor a global core.hooksPath in the publish guard

impact_assessment.why: hook_path reads only .git/config for normal repositories, while git also honors core.hooksPath from global/system config and includes; the guard then installs in .git/hooks where git never looks.
impact_assessment.benefits: A global or included hooksPath is honored, so the guard cannot be bypassed by Git configuration outside the repository.

[1/2] Review the last 18 pushes: keep the existing hook when a guard install fails

impact_assessment.why: install_pre_push_hook moves the original hook to pre-push.local and then writes the guard with Path.write_text; a disk error or crash between the two leaves no active pre-push hook, silently reopening raw pushes.
impact_assessment.benefits: The guard is written to a same-directory temp file first and atomically replaces the target, so a failed install preserves the original hook and never leaves a partial script.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: publish guard install; dependency: stdlib; concurrency: same-name temp per process; state: git_guard.py, tests, ADR, codebase map
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first failed-write test, targeted guard tests, full suite, read-only gates, verify_commit before push

[1/2] Integrate the concurrent Windows Git config discovery into the pushed guard

impact_assessment.why: The pushed guard reads %PROGRAMDATA%\\Git\\config, but Git for Windows keeps its system config beside the executable at <install>/etc/gitconfig; the concurrent work found the more reliable path.
impact_assessment.benefits: The guard finds the real system config on standard Git for Windows installs and drops the PROGRAMDATA allowlist entry.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: guard config search; dependency: stdlib shutil; concurrency: overlapping uncommitted work in the main checkout; state: git_guard.py, tests, reachability allowlist, ADR, map
impact_assessment.mitigation: apply only the Windows discovery hunk over the pushed atomic install, targeted tests, reachability, full unit tier

[1/2] Review the newest pushes: refuse a delegate transcript append when the lock times out

impact_assessment.why: append_event ignores file_lock's acquired result, so a 3-second timeout appends without serialization and can duplicate seq numbers or interleave lines.
impact_assessment.benefits: A timed-out lock now raises before any read or append; the transcript sequence stays serialized.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: delegate transcript append; dependency: stdlib; concurrency: lock contention; state: delegate_transcript.py, tests, ADR, map
